# 3. Payload Setting

**Goal:** Enter the add-on's **mass** and **X/Y/Z offset** in RBQGUI so the robot accounts for it during walking.

**Prerequisites:** Step 2 [Rail & Spring Nut](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/rail-spring-nut.html) is complete — the add-on is physically mounted on the rail.


## Before You Start

- Place the robot on a **flat, safe surface**.
- RBQGUI is **connected** to the robot ([Controller & Wi-Fi](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/controller-wifi-connect.html) complete).
- You have measured the add-on's **center-of-mass offset (X / Y / Z, in meters)** from the robot body center.

## Procedure

1. Open **Payload Configuration** in RBQGUI.
2. Enter the values in the top input fields:
   - **Mass (kg)** — payload mass
   - **Offset X / Y / Z (m)** — payload center position in the robot frame

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/troubleshooting/payload-1.png' alt='Payload Configuration input screen' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Payload Configuration — input</figcaption>
</figure>

3. Click **+ Add** to add the values to the **Added Payload** list.
4. Confirm the values are correct, then click **Set Payload**.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/troubleshooting/payload-2.png' alt='Added Payload list with entered values' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Added Payload list</figcaption>
</figure>

5. When the confirmation popup appears, verify the mass/offset and click **Confirm** to apply.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/troubleshooting/payload-3.png' alt='Payload application confirmation dialog' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Apply confirmation</figcaption>
</figure>

6. Optionally, click **Load Payload** to read back the value currently applied on the robot and verify it matches.

## Button Reference

| Button | Function |
|---|---|
| **+ Add** | Add entered mass/offset to the candidate list |
| **Clear** | Clear current input fields |
| **Set Payload** | Apply the Added Payload list to the robot |
| **Load Payload** | Read back the payload value currently applied on the robot |
| **Reset Payload** | Reset payload to default (no payload) |

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>Updating payload alone is not enough — the next step (ZMP calibration) re-centers the robot's standing posture so it actually balances under the new load.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Next Step

After registering the payload, run ZMP calibration to balance under the new weight:

**[→ 4. ZMP Calibration](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/zmp-calibration.html)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/rail-spring-nut.html
================================================================================

# 2. Rail & Spring Nut

**Goal:** Mount your add-on hardware to the robot's top rail using spring nuts.

**Prerequisites:** Step 1 [Specifications Check](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/specifications.html) is complete — the add-on is within payload and interface limits.


## What You Need

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Spring nuts** | MISUMI **SHNTP5-5** ([KR](https://kr.misumi-ec.com/vona2/detail/110302608410/?HissuCode=SHNTP5-5&PNSearch=SHNTP5-5&searchFlow=results2products&list=PageSearchResult) · [US](https://us.misumi-ec.com/vona2/detail/110302247640/?PNSearch=SHNTP5-5&HissuCode=SHNTP5-5&seriesCode=110302247640&tab=drawingAndSpecifications&Page=1)) |
| **Bolts** | M5 bolts that match your add-on's mounting holes |
| **Rigid rod** | **≤ 4 mm diameter**, for removal |

The robot top uses rails for mounting optional hardware (PTZ cameras, LiDAR, custom brackets). Spring nuts inserted into the rail slot give you threaded anchor points for M5 bolts.

## Insert a Spring Nut

1. **Insert at an angle** — slide the spring nut **diagonally** into the rail slot so it enters the internal channel.
2. **Press the protruding section** — a portion of the nut may sit proud of the slot; press it down so the nut seats fully.
3. **Align with the rail** — adjust the nut so it is aligned with the slot and can slide freely along the rail.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/insert-1.png' alt='Step 1 - diagonal insert' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 1 — diagonal insert</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/insert-2.png' alt='Step 2 - press the protruding section' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 2 — press the protruding section</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/insert-3.png' alt='Step 3 - align with the slot' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 3 — align with the slot</figcaption>
</figure>

Slide the nut to the position where your add-on bracket should sit, then tighten the M5 bolt to fix the bracket.

## Remove a Spring Nut

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p><strong>Tool diameter:</strong> use a rigid rod <strong>no larger than 4 mm</strong> in diameter. A thicker tool can damage the nut or mar the rail slot.</p>
</div>
</div>

1. **Insert a rod** — pass a rigid rod (**≤ 4 mm**) through the hole in the spring nut.
2. **Push against one wall** — push the nut against one inner wall of the rail slot.
3. **Twist and lift** — while holding it against that wall, twist and lift toward the opposite side so the nut clears the rail profile.
4. **Remove** — withdraw the nut from the slot.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/remove-1.png' alt='Step 1 - rod through the hole' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 1 — rod through the hole</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/remove-2.png' alt='Step 2 - push to one wall' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 2 — push to one wall</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/remove-3.png' alt='Step 3 - twist and lift' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 3 — twist and lift</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/remove-4.png' alt='Step 4 - remove' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 4 — remove</figcaption>
</figure>

## Next Step

Hardware is mounted. Now register the add-on's mass and offset in the GUI:

**[→ 3. Payload Setting](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/payload-setting.html)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/specifications.html

# 1. Specifications Check

**Goal:** Verify your add-on (camera, LiDAR, computer, sensor, etc.) is within the robot's mechanical and electrical limits **before** attaching it.

**Prerequisites:** None. Run this check first whenever you plan to install a new module.


## Key Limits for RBQ 10

| Parameter | Limit | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **Max Payload** | **15 kg** | Total mass of everything mounted on top of the robot |
| **Mounting interface** | **Top rail (slot)** + spring nuts | Use rail slots for repeatable, secure mounting |
| **Power available** | **54 V**, **12 V** | Check your add-on's input voltage / current draw |
| **Data interfaces** | **CAN ×1**, **Gigabit LAN ×3** | Match your add-on's communication interface |
| **Ingress Protection** | **IP54** | Add-ons should not compromise IP rating in field use |

For the full specification table (dimensions, walking speed, slope, sensors, etc.), see the manual page below.

**[→ Full Specifications (manual)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/product-descriptions/general-specification.html)**

## Pre-installation Checklist

Before moving to the next step, confirm:

- [ ] Add-on mass + any existing payload **≤ 15 kg**
- [ ] Center of mass is **roughly above the robot body** (avoid large overhang)
- [ ] Power and data interfaces match what RBQ 10 provides
- [ ] You have **measured the X / Y / Z offset** of the add-on's center of mass from the robot body center (needed in step 3)

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>Exceeding the <strong>15 kg</strong> payload limit or mounting mass far from the body center can destabilize walking, increase joint load, and shorten component life. Always check the spec sheet first.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Next Step

When your add-on passes the checklist, mount it to the rail:

**[→ 2. Rail & Spring Nut](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/rail-spring-nut.html)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/zmp-calibration.html
================================================================================

# 4. ZMP Calibration

**Goal:** Re-center the robot's Zero Moment Point so it stays balanced while standing and walking under the **new add-on weight**.

**Prerequisites:** Step 3 [Payload Setting](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/add-on/payload-setting.html) is complete — mass and X/Y/Z offset are registered in the robot.


## What ZMP Calibration Does

ZMP (Zero Moment Point) calibration aligns the center of ground reaction force while the robot is standing, so the robot can maintain balance during walking. Whenever you change payload, the center of mass shifts — this step compensates for it.

## Before You Start

- Place the robot on a **flat, solid surface**.
- Make sure **no objects or people are touching the robot**.
- RBQGUI is connected to the robot and the new payload is registered.

## Procedure

1. Launch **RBQGUI** and connect to the robot.
2. Set the robot to **Stance** (standing) mode.
3. **Press and hold** the **Sit** button.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/troubleshooting/zmp-cal-1.png" alt="Sit button" style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 3 — press and hold Sit</figcaption>
</figure>

4. In the menu that appears, select **ZMP CALIBRATE**.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/troubleshooting/zmp-cal-2.png" alt="ZMP CALIBRATE selection (Recovery menu)" style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 4 — ZMP CALIBRATE</figcaption>
</figure>

5. When the button turns **orange**, calibration is in progress.
6. **Do not touch the robot** until calibration finishes.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/troubleshooting/zmp-cal-3.png" alt="Calibration in progress (ZMP Init)" style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 5 — calibration in progress</figcaption>
</figure>

7. When the button returns to **white** and the display shows **Gait: Stance**, calibration is complete.
8. Move the robot (Stance → Walk) and verify it walks normally with the new add-on.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Do not place objects on the robot or push the robot during calibration. If calibration fails, repeat the procedure.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Done

Your add-on is mounted, registered, and the robot is calibrated for the new load. You can now command motions normally — return to **[Basic Motion Command](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/basic-motion-command.html)** to drive the robot.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/basic-motion-command.html
================================================================================

# 4. Basic Motion Command

**Goal:** Use RBQGUI and the joystick to command the robot through its basic motion modes.

**Prerequisites:** [Auto Start](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/controller-wifi-connect.html#auto-start) must be completed (all items green).

<div class="sb sb-danger">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">DANGER</p>
<p>Keep all people and animals at least 2 m away from the robot before and during operation. Never touch the robot while it is moving.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Sit Mode

The robot lowers itself into a stable seated position. Joystick input is ignored in this state.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/eqR7WaP2d-o" title="Sit mode" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Sit mode</figcaption>
</figure>

Use **Sit** to safely place the robot down before packing, charging, or any pause in operation.

## Stance Mode

- If currently **sitting** → the robot stands up.
- If currently **walking or in stair mode** → the robot stops and stands in place.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/6QEGjlFkftI" title="Stance mode" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Stance mode</figcaption>
</figure>

| Joystick | Input | Robot Action |
|---|---|---|
| L Stick | Forward / Backward | Nose up / down (pitch) |
| L Stick | Left / Right | Roll left / right |
| R Stick | Forward / Backward | Body height up / down |
| R Stick | Left / Right | Turn left / right |

## Walk Mode

The robot walks in the direction commanded by the joystick.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/x3d95WWxFF0" title="Walk mode" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Walk mode</figcaption>
</figure>

| Joystick | Input | Robot Action |
|---|---|---|
| L Stick | Forward / Backward | Move forward / backward |
| L Stick | Left / Right | Strafe left / right |
| R Stick | Forward / Backward | Pitch forward / backward |
| R Stick | Left / Right | Turn left / right |

## Stair Mode

The robot adjusts its walking speed and body lean angle automatically based on the slope of stairs.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>In Stair mode, the <strong>R Stick Forward/Backward</strong> input is not used.</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dq6S16V7oyE" title="Stair mode" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Stair mode</figcaption>
</figure>

| Joystick | Input | Robot Action |
|---|---|---|
| L Stick | Forward / Backward | Move forward / backward |
| L Stick | Left / Right | Strafe left / right |
| R Stick | Left / Right | Turn left / right |

## Docking Mode

The robot autonomously aligns itself with the docking station and initiates charging once docked.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Do not manually move the robot while Docking Mode is active. Ensure the docking station is properly positioned and powered before activating this mode.</p>
</div>
</div>

## RL (Vision Trot) Mode

The robot uses a vision-based reinforcement learning policy to walk. The policy responds dynamically to terrain using the onboard camera, making it suitable for uneven or unpredictable surfaces.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2E51kvZPB2k" title="RL vision trot mode" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">RL (Vision Trot) mode</figcaption>
</figure>

| Joystick | Input | Robot Action |
|---|---|---|
| L Stick | Forward / Backward | Move forward / backward |
| L Stick | Left / Right | Strafe left / right |
| R Stick | Left / Right | Turn left / right |

## Walking Parameter Settings

You can fine-tune the robot's walking behavior in real time from the GUI.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2DynPHB6U64" title="Walking parameter setting" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Walking parameter setting</figcaption>
</figure>

<img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/walking-parameter-set.png' alt='Walking parameter settings panel in RBQGUI' />

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| **Max Command Speed** | Limits the maximum walking speed |
| **Body Height** | Adjusts the robot's vertical posture for terrain clearance |
| **Foot Height** | Controls how high the feet lift during the swing phase |

## Next Step

Check the robot's real-time sensor and system state:

**[→ 5. State Monitoring](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/state-monitoring.html)**

# 6-1. Charging

**Goal:** Safely charge the RBQ10 battery after use.

The RBQ10 supports three charging methods:
- **Charger** — connect directly to the charging port on the top of the robot
- **Docking station** — autonomous docking and charging via the bottom port
- **External cable from docking station** — connect the station's cable to the robot's top port manually

**Prerequisites:** The robot must be powered off before connecting any charging cable.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>Charge the robot only with the supplied RBQ10 charger or RBQ10 docking station.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Charging with the RBQ10 charger

  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-1.png" alt="Charging with RBQ10 power supply" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ RBQ10 charger ]</figcaption>
</figure>

#### Step 1: Align the keying.

<p>When the robot recognizes a QR code, the docking sequence starts automatically.</p>

## Charging with an external cable from the docking station

<div class="image-group" style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; text-align: center; margin-top: 1rem; margin-bottom: 1rem;">
  <figure style="flex: 1; margin: 0;">
    <img style="max-width: 95%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/description-2.png" alt="Docking station external charge port" />
    <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ External charging port ]</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure style="flex: 1; margin: 0;">
    <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/description-3.png" alt="External charging cable" />
    <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ External charging cable ]</figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>

### How to charge

#### Step 1: Connect the external charging cable to the RBQ10 docking station external charging port.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-4.png" alt="Docking external cable step 1" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Connect cable to external charging port ]</figcaption>
</figure>

#### Step 2: Connect the external charging cable to the RBQ10 charging port.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-2.png" alt="Cable to robot charge port step 2" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Connect cable to robot charging port ]</figcaption>
</figure>

#### Step 3: Charge the RBQ10 using the docking station external charging cable.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-6.png" alt="Charging via dock external cable step 3" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Charge robot with external cable ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Docking station installation precautions

1. The charging station is water-resistant, but if water is present on the charging terminals, charging problems may occur; install it away from places where water splashes.
2. The power cable is treated for water exposure, but when connecting to an external outlet, keep water out of the plug connection.
3. Prolonged direct sunlight can cause overheating; installing in a shaded location is recommended.
4. Secure the charging station to the floor using the fixing holes.

## Next Step

When the robot is fully charged, pack it for storage or transport:

**[→ 6-2. Packing](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/packing.html)**

# 2. Controller & Wi-Fi Connection

**Goal:** Connect the Steam Deck controller to the robot Wi-Fi, link RBQGUI to the robot, and complete Auto Start so the robot is ready to operate.

**Prerequisites:** [Initial Pose & Power On](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/initial-pose.html) must be completed first — the robot must be on and initialized.

## Step 1: Open RBQGUI app

Run the `RBQGUI` app from the STEAM DECK desktop.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-open-app.png' alt='RBQGUI app' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ RBQGUI app ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Step 2: Wi-Fi connection

The robot provides a Wi-Fi access point named `RBQ_{XX}` (XX differs by unit). Connect the STEAM DECK to that network.

1. **Check Wi-Fi** - After connecting the Steam Deck to the robot AP (`RBQ_{XX}`), confirm the **top-right** of RBQGUI shows the network name and signal icon.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-wifi-1.png' alt='Wi-Fi status in RBQGUI' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Wi-Fi menu ]</figcaption>
</figure>

2. **Select the robot network** - Choose `RBQ_{XX}` in the list. (If it does not appear, check robot power and Wi-Fi operation.)

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-wifi-2.png' alt='Select RBQ_XX network' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Select RBQ_{XX} ]</figcaption>
</figure>

3. **Verify connection** - Confirm the deck shows **Connected** to `RBQ_{XX}`.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-wifi-3.png' alt='RBQ_XX connected' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Wi-Fi connected ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Step 3: Connect STEAM DECK and robot

For RBQGUI to talk to the robot, you must also establish remote controller-robot communication inside the app.

1. **Open the connection dialog** - Press `Remote Controller-Robot Communication Connection` (orange) on the left of the top bar. A connection pop-up appears.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-connect-1.png' alt='Remote controller-robot communication connection' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Communication connection button and pop-up ]</figcaption>
</figure>

2. **Connect** - In the pop-up, press `Connect` to attempt communication with the robot.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-connect-2.png' alt='Connect button' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Connect ]</figcaption>
</figure>

3. **Confirm result** - When connected, `Remote Controller-Robot Communication Connection` at the same position turns **green**, and the pop-up shows a connected state.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-connect-3.png' alt='Connected to robot' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Connected (button green) ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Step 4: Auto start {#auto-start}

To bring up robot software and state in one flow, use the auto start procedure.

1. **Open initial setup** - Press `Robot Initial Setup` (red) on the left of the top bar.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/auto-start-1.png' alt='Robot Initial Setup' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Robot Initial Setup button ]</figcaption>
</figure>

2. **Run auto start** - In the pop-up, press `Auto Start Robot`. After a short wait, progress appears on screen.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/auto-start-2.png' alt='Auto Start Robot' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Auto Start Robot ]</figcaption>
</figure>

3. **Check progress** - Confirm each item such as `Manual Setup` updates. (Some items may show green before others for a while.)

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/auto-start-3.png' alt='Auto start in progress' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Auto start in progress ]</figcaption>
</figure>

4. **Confirm completion** - When **all** setup items shown on screen are **green**, auto start has completed successfully.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/auto-start-4.png' alt='Auto start complete' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Auto start complete (all green) ]</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>If, after auto start, not all setup items turn green or an error is shown, confirm no people are nearby, review the <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/safety/emergency-stop-procedures.html">emergency stop procedures</a>, then follow the steps below. Before operation, always comply with the <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/safety/general-safety-warning-precautions.html">general safety guidelines</a>.</p>
<ol style="margin: 0.5rem 0 0 1.25rem;">
<li>If <code>Check CAN-Bus</code> fails: power off the robot safely, then restart.</li>
<li>If <code>Find Home-pose</code> fails: on a flat, stable surface per <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/safety/maintenance-safety.html">maintenance safety</a>, check leg pose, then restart.</li>
</ol>
<p style="margin-top: 0.75rem;">If the problem persists, contact Rainbow Robotics via <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/troubleshooting/error-reporting.html">error reporting</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Next Step

The robot is connected. Get familiar with the RBQGUI screen and buttons:

**[→ 3. GUI Introduction](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/gui-introduction.html)**

# 6-3. Emergency Stop & Recovery

**Goal:** Know how to stop the robot immediately in an emergency and how to safely resume operation.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>Always keep the emergency stop button accessible during operation. In any situation where the robot poses a risk to people or property, press the emergency stop button immediately.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Physical Emergency Stop Button

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/emo.png' alt='Emergency stop button on the rear of the robot' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Emergency stop push button — located on the rear of the robot ]</figcaption>
</figure>

When the **emergency stop button** is pressed:

- All joints switch to **High Damping** mode.
- The robot resists external motion but does **not** accept torque or position commands.
- The robot may lose its posture and settle to the ground under gravity.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>High Damping mode protects both the user and the robot. The robot will not execute any motion commands until the emergency stop is cleared and the robot is re-initialized.</p>
</div>
</div>

## GUI Emergency Stop

You can also trigger an emergency stop from RBQGUI without reaching the physical button.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/safety/emergency-button-gui.png' alt='Emergency stop button in RBQGUI' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ EMERGENCY button in RBQGUI top bar ]</figcaption>
</figure>

Pressing the **EMERGENCY** button in the top bar of RBQGUI has the same effect as the physical button — all joints enter High Damping mode immediately.

## Recovery Procedure

After an emergency stop, follow these steps to safely resume operation:

1. **Ensure safety** — Confirm that all people and animals have moved at least 2 m away from the robot.
2. **Release the button** — Rotate the physical emergency stop button clockwise to return it to its original (unlocked) position.
3. **Return to initial pose** — If the robot has fallen or shifted, manually return it to the [correct initial pose](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/initial-pose.html) on a flat surface.
4. **Re-initialize** — Press the **Stance** button in RBQGUI, or run **Auto Start** from the [Controller & Wi-Fi](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/controller-wifi-connect.html#auto-start) setup.
5. **Verify** — Confirm that the EMERGENCY indicator is no longer lit and that all Auto Start items are green before resuming operation.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Do not attempt to force-move the joints while the robot is in High Damping mode. Return the robot to the initial pose carefully and only after the emergency stop has been released.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Related

- [General Safety Guidelines](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/safety/general-safety-warning-precautions.html)
- [Emergency Stop Procedures (detailed)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/safety/emergency-stop-procedures.html)

# 3. GUI Introduction

**Goal:** Get familiar with the RBQGUI screen layout and key buttons before sending motion commands.

**Prerequisites:** [Controller & Wi-Fi Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/controller-wifi-connect.html) must be completed — RBQGUI should be linked to the robot.


## Main Screen

After Auto Start completes, the RBQGUI main screen looks like this:

<figure style="margin-top: 0; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/introduction.png' alt='RBQGUI main screen' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem;">&lt;RBQGUI main screen&gt;</figcaption>
</figure>

RBQGUI provides three core capabilities:

- **Connection** — Communicates with the robot on the same Wi-Fi network.
- **Control** — Selects gait modes (sit, stance, walk, stair, docking, RL) and drives the robot via the joystick.
- **Monitoring** — Shows battery, sensor, and connection status on screen.

## Button Reference (1–9)

| No. | Function |
|---:|---|
| 1 | **Sit** — keep the robot in a sitting pose |
| 2 | **Stance** — stand up to the default pose |
| 3 | **Walk** — walk (forward/back, strafe, turn) |
| 4 | **Stair** — gait suited for stairs |
| 5 | **Docking** — align to the charging dock |
| 6 | **RL (Vision Trot)** — vision-based RL walking |
| 7 | **Walking Parameter Setting** — tune speed, body height, foot lift |
| 8 | **3D Virtual View** — switch to the 3D virtual view |
| 9 | **Camera View** — switch to the live camera view |

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>When the robot posture or the app view changes, the corresponding button turns orange.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Next Step

Now that you know what each button does, try the basic motion commands:

**[→ 4. Basic Motion Command](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/basic-motion-command.html)**

SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/initial-pose.html

# 1. Initial Pose & Power On

**Goal:** Place the robot in the correct initial pose on a flat surface, then power it on.

<div class="sb sb-required">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-book" aria-hidden="true">📖</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">REQUIRED READING</p>
<p>Before operating the robot, read the <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/safety/general-safety-warning-precautions.html">General Safety Guidelines</a> and the <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/safety/indications.html">Safety Indications</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Prerequisites

- A flat, stable floor with sufficient open space (minimum 2 m radius clearance around the robot)
- The robot battery is charged
- No people or animals within 2 m of the robot

## Setting the Initial Pose

Place the robot on the floor so that all feet and knees contact the ground simultaneously.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/initial-pose-1.png' alt='RBQ10 correct initial pose overview' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ RBQ10 Initial Pose ]</figcaption>
</figure>

### Step 1. Choose a flat surface

Place the robot on a level floor. Uneven surfaces can cause Auto Start to fail.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/initial-pose-2.png' alt='Flat surface requirement' />
</figure>

### Step 2. Fully fold the knee joints

Fold all four knee joints completely so the knee pads are close to the ground.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/initial-pose-3.png' alt='Fold knee joints' />
</figure>

### Step 3. Set all three ground contact points

Rotate the hip pitch and roll joints until **three points per leg** contact the floor: the **body bumper**, the **knee joint**, and the **foot**.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/initial-pose-4.png' alt='Three ground contact points' />
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>If the initial pose is incorrect, Auto Start will fail and the robot may fall unexpectedly. Always confirm all contact points before powering on.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Power On

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/power-button.png" alt="Power button" style="width: 300px;" />
</figure>

1. Press the **Power Button** on the robot body.
2. Confirm the **red indicator** light on the button turns on.
3. Listen for the **double-beep** sound — this confirms the boot sequence has started.

The robot will take about 30–60 seconds to fully initialize. Do not attempt to move the robot during this time.

## Next Step

Once the robot is on and initialized, proceed to connect the controller and Wi-Fi:

**[→ 2. Controller & Wi-Fi Connection](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/controller-wifi-connect.html)**

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/packing.html
================================================================================

# 6-2. Packing

**Goal:** Safely pack the RBQ10 into its Pelican case for storage or transport.

**Prerequisites:** The robot is powered off and all additional attached equipment has been removed.

The RBQ10 is stored and transported using a **Pelican 1730 Protector Case**. The model of the Pelican case used is the 1730 Protector Case. Please refer to the images below and store the RBQ10 along with other items accordingly.


## Robot packing and unpacking
The Pelican case has two layers. The lower layer holds the charger, spare rubber feet, and LiDAR; the RBQ10 is placed on top of them.
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-1.png' alt='Pelican case lower layer layout' />
</figure>

After arranging items in the lower layer, carry the robot as shown in the figure and place it in the case.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>The robot must be carried by two people working together.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Before transporting the robot, remove any additional equipment attached to it and turn off the power.</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-2.png' alt='Carrying robot into case' />
</figure>

After setting the RBQ10 on the floor, extend the legs as shown in the figure.

Two people should carry the robot, each holding one of the leg areas marked in red.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-3.png' alt='Transport with legs extended' />
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Be careful not to let any foreign objects get into the knee joint rotation area, and ensure fingers do not get pinched!</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-4.png' alt='Knee joint caution pose' />
</figure>

Place the robot in the Pelican 1730 case to match the case shape.

After the body is in the case, fold the legs in this order:

### Step 1: Fold the front legs’ knee joints fully
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-5.png' alt='Front leg knee fold step 1' />
</figure>

### Step 2: Rotate the front legs’ hip pitch joints and place the legs into the case recesses

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-6.png' alt='Front leg hip pitch rotation step 2' />
</figure>
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-7.png' alt='Front leg placed in case step 2 (continued)' />
</figure>

### Step 3: Rotate the rear legs’ hip pitch joints so the legs go over the front thighs

### Step 4: Fully extend the rear shins
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-8.png' alt='Rear leg shin extension step 4' />
</figure>

Place the remote controller in the side storage next to the robot. Remaining empty space can be used as needed.

Close the lid to finish packing.

Unpacking is the reverse of the above steps.


## Packing Dimension

# 5. State Monitoring

**Goal:** Understand how to read the robot's real-time status panels in RBQGUI.

In RBQGUI, the State Monitoring view shows emergency status, battery level, sensor readings, and module health — all in one screen.

## Top Status Bar

The top bar shows the **EMERGENCY** state indicator, battery voltage, connection status, and other system icons at a glance.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/state-monitoring-1.png' alt='Top status bar' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Top status bar — EMERGENCY, battery, connection indicators</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>If the <strong>EMERGENCY</strong> indicator is lit, stop all operation immediately and follow the <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/emo.html">Emergency Stop & Recovery</a> procedure before continuing.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Joint & Sensor Diagnostics

The diagnostics table shows per-joint values (temperature, position error, etc.) and IMU readings (gyro, acceleration) for every leg.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/state-monitoring-2.png' alt='Joint and sensor diagnostics table' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Joint/sensor diagnostics table</figcaption>
</figure>

### Joint naming convention

| Abbreviation | Joint |
|---|---|
| HRR / HRP / HRK | Hind Right — Roll / Pitch / Knee |
| HLR / HLP / HLK | Hind Left — Roll / Pitch / Knee |
| FRR / FRP / FRK | Front Right — Roll / Pitch / Knee |
| FLR / FLP / FLK | Front Left — Roll / Pitch / Knee |

## Perception Module Status

This panel shows the on/off state of vision and sensor modules (IR projector, night vision, LED, buzzer, etc.) and reports operation/error/count values (Fail / Count).

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/state-monitoring-3.png' alt='Perception module status panel' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Perception module status</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>If a perception module shows <strong>OFF</strong> or reports errors, vision-based features such as RL (Vision Trot) mode may be unavailable or unreliable.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Power Switch & Module Check

This panel displays power-switch states for the Vision Computer, cameras, LiDAR, and other peripherals, as well as load readings for BAT / LEGS / ADDON / EXTERN / CHARGE.

Use **Reset** to clear counters and **Check** to refresh status.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/state-monitoring-4.png' alt='Power switch and module health check panel' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Power switch & module check</figcaption>
</figure>

## Next Step

After verifying the robot is healthy, proceed to charge or pack it for storage:

- **[→ 6-1. Charging](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/charging.html)**
- **[→ 6-2. Packing](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/packing.html)**
- **[→ 6-3. Emergency Stop & Recovery](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/emo.html)**

# Developer Setup Guide

**Goal:** Clone the RBQ repository, set up the development environment, and launch the simulator so you can test robot behavior before running on hardware.

<div class="sb sb-required">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-book" aria-hidden="true">📖</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">REQUIRED READING</p>
<p>Familiarize yourself with the safety guidelines before testing on the real robot: <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/safety/general-safety-warning-precautions.html">General Safety Guidelines</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>

## System Requirements

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| OS | Ubuntu 22.04 (x86-64) |
| CPU | Intel Core i7 12th Gen or equivalent |
| RAM | 16 GB or more |
| Storage | 25 GB free space |
| Control | Keyboard (W/A/S/D/Q/E/R/F, 1–5) or Logitech F710 gamepad |

## Step 1. Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RainbowRobotics/RBQ.git
cd RBQ
```

> All SDK source code, examples, scripts, and simulator environments live inside `RBQ/`.  
> Run all commands from this directory unless stated otherwise.

> **Note:** Pre-built binaries are already included in `bin/`. No compilation step is required to run the simulator or deploy to the robot.

## Step 2. Launch the Simulator

Start the RBQ control stack, MuJoCo physics simulator, and RBQGUI together:

```bash
bash scripts/sim.bash          # motion only
bash scripts/sim.bash --vision # motion + vision sensors
```

If prompted, enter your user password in the newly opened terminal windows.

## Step 3. Connect and Initialize in RBQGUI

1. In RBQGUI, click **Connect** — the indicator changes to **Simulator Connected** (blue).
2. Click **Auto Start Robot** — all indicators turn green when ready.
3. In the **Walk** tab, press **Stance** (or keyboard `2`) to stand the robot up.

The robot is now ready to receive commands. Refer to [Basic Motion Command](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/basic-motion-command.html) for joystick and gait control.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>In simulation, only <strong>Control Start</strong> turns green. On the real robot, all three startup indicators (Motor Check / Initialize Pose / Control Start) turn green when ready.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Step 4. Run on the Real Robot

When you are ready to test on hardware:

1. Place the robot in the [correct initial pose](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/common/initial-pose.html).
2. Connect your development PC to the robot Wi-Fi (`RBQ_xxxx`).
3. Launch the GUI (from `RBQ/`):

```bash
./bin/GUI
```

4. Click **Connect** → **Auto Start Robot** → **Stance**.

> It is strongly recommended to verify all behaviors in simulation before testing on the real robot.

## Step 5. Update the Robot

Robot software is updated from RBQGUI, using **`UPDATE ROBOT`** on the `Software Update`
screen. RBQGUI transfers and installs the new version, then prompts you to restart.

**→ [Robot Software Update](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/robot-software-update.html)**

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Put the robot in the <strong>sitting</strong> state before restarting, and do not move it until the restart finishes. Running a mismatched binary and script combination can cause unexpected behavior.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Detailed Reference

| Topic | Link |
|---|---|
| Full GUI walkthrough | [Developers Guide (Software)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/developers-guide.html) |
| GUI panel details | [GUI Introduction](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/introduction.html) |
| Simulation environment | [MuJoCo Simulation](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/developers-guide.html#simulation) |
| Concepts & architecture | [Concept](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/concept.html) |

SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/high-level.html

# High Level Command — Quick Start

**Source**: `rbq_sdk/cpp/example/src/rbq_high_level.cpp`

Publishes `HighLevelCommand` at 50 Hz. Type gait names in the terminal; control velocity with a joystick.

## Build

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/cpp/example
bash scripts/setup.bash
bash scripts/build.bash
```

## Run

```bash
./bin/rbq_high_level <networkInterface> [joystickPath]
./bin/rbq_high_level eth0
```

A joystick is required. The program auto-detects `/dev/input/js*` (prefers Logitech/Xbox by name).  
Override with an explicit path: `./bin/rbq_high_level eth0 /dev/input/js1`

## Terminal usage

```
list              ← print the example's built-in list
standing          ← switch by name
3                 ← switch by ID (trotting)
waving            ← switch to wave gait
```

## Supported gaits

| Name | ID | Notes |
|------|----|-------|
| `sitting` | 0 | Sit down |
| `standing` | 1 | Default at startup |
| `trotting` | 3 | MPC trot |
| `trot_stairs` | 4 | Stair-climbing trot |
| `waving` | 5 | Wave gait |
| `docking` | 10 | Auto-docking sequence |

> The example's built-in list also prints internal gaits that are not supported. Use only the gaits in the table above.

## Joystick velocity

| Axis | Command | Max |
|------|---------|-----|
| L stick forward/back | `vel_x` | ±1.2 m/s |
| L stick left/right | `vel_y` | ±0.5 m/s |
| R stick left/right | `omega_z` | ±60 deg/s |

> `omega_z` is in **deg/s** — QuadWalk converts to rad/s internally.

## Important

The program sends `switchControlMode = true` at startup.  
Without this, the robot ignores `HighLevelCommand` and stays in joystick mode.

→ **Full reference**: [High Level Command](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/cpp/high-level.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/low-level.html
================================================================================

# Low Level (RL Policy) — Quick Start

**Source**: `rbq_sdk/cpp/example/src/rbq_low_level.cpp`

Runs a learned walking policy (ONNX) on the robot at 100 Hz via low-level joint control.

## Build

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/cpp/example
bash scripts/setup.bash
bash scripts/build.bash
```

## Run

From `RBQ/rbq_sdk/cpp/example/`:

```bash
# Use sudo for real-time thread; without sudo = normal thread
sudo ./bin/rbq_low_level -p ../../rbq_simulator/rbq_gym/policy/rbq10/
```

`-p` is **required** — pass a directory containing `info.json` and `policy.onnx`.

## Run with simulation

1. From `RBQ/` root, start the simulator:
   ```bash
   bash scripts/sim.bash
   ```
2. In RBQGUI: **Connect** → **Auto Start Robot** → **Stance** (key `2`).
3. Run the example:
   ```bash
   sudo ./bin/rbq_low_level -p ../../rbq_simulator/rbq_gym/policy/rbq10/
   ```

## Keyboard controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `x` | Stand up (ready posture) |
| `z` | Sit down (ground posture) |
| `c` | Start walking (loads policy) |
| `q` | Quit |

## Policy directory

Pre-trained policies are in the repository at:
```
rbq_simulator/rbq_gym/policy/rbq10/
├── info.json
└── policy.onnx
```

Trained your own policy with [Isaac Gym](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/simulator/rbq-gym.html) or [Isaac Lab](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/simulator/rbq-lab.html)?  
Point `-p` at the exported directory (`policy.onnx` + `info.json`).

## State machine

| State | How to enter | What happens |
|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Idle | (default) | Mirrors the stack's final reference |
| Motion | `x` or `z` | Interpolates to ready / ground posture |
| Control | `c` | Runs ONNX policy at 100 Hz, publishes joint references |

→ **Full reference**: [Low Level (RL Policy)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/cpp/low-level.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/quick-start.html
================================================================================

# RBQ C++ SDK — Quick Start

Get the SDK built and your first example running in 5 steps.

## 1. Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RainbowRobotics/RBQ.git
cd RBQ
```

> All scripts, SDK source code, and examples are in the repository root. Run all commands from `RBQ/` unless stated otherwise.

## 2. Build the C++ SDK

```bash
cd rbq_sdk/cpp/rbq_sdk_cpp

# First time only — build bundled CycloneDDS
sudo bash scripts/build_dds.bash

# Build and install the SDK
sudo bash scripts/build.bash

cd ../../..
```

## 3. Build the examples

```bash
cd rbq_sdk/cpp/example

# Install build dependencies (first time only)
bash scripts/setup.bash

# Build examples
bash scripts/build.bash

cd ../../..
```

Binaries are placed in `rbq_sdk/cpp/example/bin/`.

## 4. Start the simulator (skip for real hardware)

From the `RBQ/` root:

```bash
bash scripts/sim.bash
```

In RBQGUI:
1. **Connect** → indicator turns blue.
2. **Auto Start Robot** → indicators turn green.
3. **Walk** tab → **Stance** (or press `2`) to stand the robot up.

## 5. Run your first example

From `rbq_sdk/cpp/example/`:

```bash
# Terminal-based command test
./bin/rbq_sport_client eth0

# Joystick control
./bin/rbq_sport_client_joy eth0

# High-level gait + velocity (requires joystick)
./bin/rbq_high_level eth0

# Low-level RL policy
sudo ./bin/rbq_low_level -p ../../rbq_simulator/rbq_gym/policy/rbq10/
```

Replace `eth0` with your network interface (`ifconfig` to check).  
For robot Wi-Fi (`RBQ_xxxx`), use the Wi-Fi interface (e.g. `wlp4s0`).

## Examples overview

| Example | Binary | What it does |
|---------|--------|-------------|
| [Sport Client →](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/sport-client.html) | `rbq_sport_client` | Terminal CLI — test any SportClient command |
| [Sport Client (Joy) →](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/sport-client-joy.html) | `rbq_sport_client_joy` | Gamepad — full button mapping |
| [High Level Cmd →](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/high-level.html) | `rbq_high_level` | 50 Hz gait + joystick velocity |
| [Low Level (Policy) →](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/low-level.html) | `rbq_low_level` | Joint control + ONNX RL policy |

→ **Build issues?** See [SDK Build Issues](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/troubleshooting/sdk-build.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/sport-client-joy.html
================================================================================

# Sport Client (Joystick) — Quick Start

**Source**: `rbq_sdk/cpp/example/src/rbq_sport_client_joy.cpp`

Gamepad-driven robot control via SportClient. Analog sticks → velocity, buttons → discrete actions.

## Build

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/cpp/example
bash scripts/setup.bash
bash scripts/build.bash
```

## Run

```bash
./bin/rbq_sport_client_joy <networkInterface> [joystickPath]
./bin/rbq_sport_client_joy eth0
./bin/rbq_sport_client_joy eth0 /dev/input/js1
```

Joystick is auto-detected from `/dev/input/js*` (prefers Logitech/Xbox by name).  
Override with `JOY=/dev/input/js1 ./bin/rbq_sport_client_joy eth0`.

## Gamepad layout (Logitech F710 / Xbox)

### Button chords

| Hold + Press | Action |
|-------------|--------|
| **L2 + B** | E-stop (Damp) |
| **L2 + A** × 1 | StandUp (lock joints) |
| **L2 + A** × 2 | StandDown (prone) |
| **START** | Default gait |
| **L2 + START** | Running mode |
| **L2 + X** | Recovery stand |
| **R1 + X** | Climb mode |
| **L1 + X** | **not supported on this robot** |
| **L1 + Y** | **not supported on this robot** |
| **BACK** | Stop move |

### Double-click (within 400 ms)

| Button | Action |
|--------|--------|
| X × 2 | Left-side gait |
| Y × 2 | Right-side gait |
| R1 × 2 | **not supported on this robot** |
| R2 × 2 | **not supported on this robot** |

### Analog sticks

| Axis | Maps to | Max |
|------|---------|-----|
| L stick forward/back | vel_x | ±0.55 m/s |
| L stick left/right | vel_y | ±0.35 m/s |
| R stick left/right | vyaw | ±1.0 rad/s |

Deadzone: 0.12 on all axes.

→ **Full reference**: [Sport Client (Joystick)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/cpp/sport-client-joy.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/sport-client.html
================================================================================

# Sport Client — Quick Start

**Source**: `rbq_sdk/cpp/example/src/rbq_sport_client.cpp`

Interactive terminal CLI that sends any SportClient command to the robot.

## Build

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/cpp/example
bash scripts/setup.bash
bash scripts/build.bash
```

## Run

```bash
./bin/rbq_sport_client <networkInterface>
# e.g.
./bin/rbq_sport_client eth0
```

## Usage

```
Input "list " to list all test option ...
list              ← print all commands
balance_stand     ← execute by name
1                 ← execute by ID
```

## Commands

| ID | Name | What it does |
|----|------|-------------|
| 0 | `damp` | High-damping e-stop |
| 1 | `balance_stand` | Balanced standing |
| 2 | `stop_move` | Stop in place |
| 3 | `stand_down` | Go prone |
| 4 | `recovery_stand` | Stand up from fall |
| 5 | `move` | Rotate in place (`Move(0, 0, 0.5)`) |
| 6 | `switch_gait` | Switch to default gait |
| 8 | `get_state` | Print FSM state / speed level / process state |
| 11 | `stand_up` | Lock joints in standing position |
| 16 | `front_flip` | **not supported on this robot** |
| 17 | `back_flip` | **not supported on this robot** |
| 18 | `pose` | Body position offset — **may not be available** |
| 19 | `euler` | Body euler angle — **may not be available** |

> Full list: type `list` at the prompt. Unknown commands print a guidance message.

## Notes

- The client uses `SetNoReply(true)` — fire-and-forget, no RPC wait.
- Loop runs at 50 Hz; the selected command executes on every tick.

→ **Full reference**: [Sport Client (Software)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/cpp/sport-client.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-python/high-level.html
================================================================================

```
3                 ← switch by ID (trotting)
waving            ← switch to wave gait
```

## Supported gaits

| Name | ID | Notes |
|------|----|-------|
| `sitting` | 0 | Sit down |
| `standing` | 1 | Default at startup |
| `trotting` | 3 | MPC trot |
| `trot_stairs` | 4 | Stair-climbing trot |
| `waving` | 5 | Wave gait |
| `docking` | 10 | Auto-docking sequence |

> The example's built-in list also prints internal gaits that are not supported. Use only the gaits in the table above.

## Joystick velocity

| Axis | Command | Max |
|------|---------|-----|
| L stick forward/back | `vel_x` | ±1.2 m/s |
| L stick left/right | `vel_y` | ±0.5 m/s |
| R stick left/right | `omega_z` | ±60 deg/s |

> `omega_z` is in **deg/s** — QuadWalk converts to rad/s internally.

## Important

The program sends `switchControlMode = true` at startup.  
Without this, the robot ignores `HighLevelCommand` and stays in joystick mode.

# Low Level (RL Policy) Python — Quick Start

**Source**: `rbq_sdk/python/example/sport/rbq_low_level.py`

Python port of the C++ `rbq_low_level` example. Loads an RL policy (`info.json` + `policy.onnx`) and drives leg joints via low-level joint control at 100 Hz.

## Install

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/python
pip install -e .
pip install onnxruntime
```

## Run

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/python/example/sport
python3 rbq_low_level.py -p <policyDir> [networkInterface]
```

```bash
# Simulation (loopback — networkInterface can be omitted)
python3 rbq_low_level.py -p ../../../../rbq_simulator/rbq_gym/policy/rbq10/

# Real robot
python3 rbq_low_level.py -p ../../../../rbq_simulator/rbq_gym/policy/rbq10/ eth0
```

`-p` is **required** — pass a directory containing `info.json` and `policy.onnx`.

> Unlike the C++ version, no `sudo` is needed (Python does not use a real-time thread).

## Run with simulation

1. From `RBQ/` root, start the simulator:
   ```bash
   bash scripts/sim.bash
   ```
2. In RBQGUI: **Connect** → **Auto Start Robot** → **Stance** (key `2`).
3. Run the example (network interface optional for loopback):
   ```bash
   python3 rbq_low_level.py -p ../../../../rbq_simulator/rbq_gym/policy/rbq10/
   ```

## Keyboard controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `x` | Stand up (ready posture) |
| `z` | Sit down (ground posture) |
| `c` | Start walking (loads and runs policy) |
| `q` | Quit |

## Policy directory

Pre-trained policies are included in the repository:

```
rbq_simulator/rbq_gym/policy/rbq10/
├── info.json
└── policy.onnx
```

Supported policy names (from `info.json`): `rbq10`, `rbq10_trot`, `rbq10_trot_run`.

Trained your own policy with [Isaac Gym](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/simulator/rbq-gym.html) or [Isaac Lab](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/simulator/rbq-lab.html)?  
Point `-p` at the exported directory (`policy.onnx` + `info.json`).

## State machine

| State | How to enter | What happens |
|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Idle | (default) | Mirrors the stack's final joint reference |
| Motion | `x` or `z` | Cosine-interpolates to ready / ground posture |
| Control | `c` | Runs ONNX policy at 100 Hz, publishes joint references |

→ **C++ version**: [Low Level (C++)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-cpp/low-level.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-python/quick-start.html
================================================================================

# RBQ Python SDK — Quick Start

Run a Python SDK example in 3 steps.

## 1. Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RainbowRobotics/RBQ.git
cd RBQ

# Install the Python SDK
cd rbq_sdk/python
pip install -e .
cd ../..
```

## 2. Start the simulator (skip for real hardware)

```bash
bash scripts/sim.bash
```

In RBQGUI: **Connect** → **Auto Start Robot** → **Stance** (`2`).

## 3. Run an example

```bash
cd rbq_sdk/python/example/sport

# Terminal CLI
python3 rbq_sport_client.py eth0

# Joystick control
python3 rbq_sport_client_joy.py eth0
```

Replace `eth0` with your network interface (`ifconfig` to check).

## Examples overview

| Example | What it does |
|---------|-------------|
| [Sport Client →](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-python/sport-client.html) | Terminal CLI — test any command |
| [Sport Client (Joy) →](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-python/sport-client-joy.html) | Gamepad — full button mapping |

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-python/sport-client-joy.html
================================================================================

# Sport Client Joystick (Python) — Quick Start

**Source**: `rbq_sdk/python/example/sport/rbq_sport_client_joy.py`

Gamepad-driven robot control via Python SportClient. Single event loop at 10 Hz.

## Install

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/python
pip install -e .
```

## Run

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/python/example/sport
python3 rbq_sport_client_joy.py <networkInterface> [joystickPath]
python3 rbq_sport_client_joy.py eth0
python3 rbq_sport_client_joy.py eth0 /dev/input/js1
```

## Gamepad layout (Logitech F710 / Xbox)

### Button chords

| Hold + Press | Action |
|-------------|--------|
| **L2 + B** | E-stop (Damp) |
| **L2 + A** × 1 | StandUp |
| **L2 + A** × 2 | StandDown |
| **START** | Default gait |
| **L2 + START** | Running mode |
| **L2 + X** | Recovery stand |
| **R1 + X** | Climb |
| **L1 + X** | **not supported on this robot** |
| **L1 + Y** | **not supported on this robot** |
| **BACK** | Stop |

### Double-click (400 ms)

| Button | Action |
|--------|--------|
| X × 2 | Left-side gait |
| Y × 2 | Right-side gait |
| R1 × 2 | **not supported on this robot** |
| R2 × 2 | **not supported on this robot** |

### Sticks (when no button)

| Axis | Command | Max |
|------|---------|-----|
| L stick forward | vel_x | ±1.0 m/s |
| L stick left | vel_y | ±0.5 m/s |
| R stick left | vyaw | ±1.0 rad/s |

→ **Full reference**: [Sport Client Joystick (Python)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/python/sport-client-joy.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-python/sport-client.html
================================================================================

# Sport Client (Python) — Quick Start

**Source**: `rbq_sdk/python/example/sport/rbq_sport_client.py`

Python terminal CLI for sending SportClient commands.

## Install

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/python
pip install -e .
```

## Run

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/python/example/sport
python3 rbq_sport_client.py <networkInterface>
# e.g.
python3 rbq_sport_client.py eth0
```

## Usage

```
Input "list " to list all test option ...
list            ← print all commands
balance_stand   ← execute by name
1               ← execute by ID
```

## Key commands

| ID | Name | What it does |
|----|------|-------------|
| 0 | `damp` | E-stop |
| 1 | `balance_stand` | Standing |
| 4 | `recovery_stand` | Stand up from fall |
| 5 | `move` | Rotate in place |
| 8 | `get_state` | Print robot state |
| 11 | `stand_up` | Lock standing joints |
| 16 | `front_flip` | **not supported on this robot** |
| 17 | `back_flip` | **not supported on this robot** |

→ **Full reference**: [Sport Client (Python)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/python/sport-client.html)

SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-ros/high-level.html

# High Level Command — Quick Start (ROS2)

**Source**: `rbq_sdk/ros2/src/rbq_examples/src/rbq_high_level.cpp`

Publishes `HighLevelCommand` at 50 Hz over ROS 2.  
Select gaits from the terminal; control velocity with a joystick.

## Build

```bash
cd RBQ/rbq_sdk/ros2
rosdep install --from-paths src -y --ignore-src
colcon build --symlink-install
source install/setup.bash
```

## Run

```bash
ros2 run rbq_examples rbq_high_level [joystickPath]
# e.g.
ros2 run rbq_examples rbq_high_level
ros2 run rbq_examples rbq_high_level /dev/input/js1
```

Default joystick path is `/dev/input/js0`.

## Terminal usage

```
list              ← print the example's built-in list
stand             ← switch by name
3                 ← switch by ID (walk)
wave              ← switch to wave gait
```

## Supported gaits

| Name | ID | Notes |
|------|----|-------|
| `sit` | 0 | Sit down |
| `stand` | 1 | Default standing |
| `walk` | 3 | MPC trot gait |
| `stairs` | 4 | Stair-adaptive gait |
| `wave` | 5 | Slow walk gait |

> The example's built-in list also prints internal gaits that are not supported. Use only the gaits in the table above.

## Joystick velocity

| Axis | Command | Max |
|------|---------|-----|
| L stick forward/back | `vel_x` | ±1.2 m/s |
| L stick left/right | `vel_y` | ±0.5 m/s |
| R stick left/right | `omega_z` | ±60 deg/s |

Deadzone: 0.12. `omega_z` is in **deg/s**.

## ROS 2 topics used

| Direction | Topic | Message type |
|-----------|-------|--------------|
| Publish | `/rbq/cmd/high_level` | `rbq_msgs/msg/HighLevelCommand` |
| Publish | `/rbq/cmd/switch_control_mode` | `std_msgs/msg/Bool` |
| Publish | `/rbq/cmd/switch_gait` | `std_msgs/msg/Int8` |
| Subscribe | `/rbq/robot_status` | `rbq_msgs/msg/RobotStatus` (best-effort QoS) |

`HighLevelCommand` posture/velocity fields (`roll`, `pitch`, `yaw`, `vel_x`, `vel_y`, `omega_z`, `delta_body_h`, `delta_foot_h`) are `float32`. See the [full field reference](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/ros/high-level.html).

## Important

At startup, `switch_control_mode = true` is sent once to enable HighLevel mode.  
Without this, the robot ignores `HighLevelCommand` and stays in joystick mode.

→ **Full reference**: [High Level Command (ROS2)](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/ros/high-level.html)

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/guides/sdk-ros/quick-start.html
================================================================================

# RBQ ROS2 SDK — Quick Start

Connect the RBQ robot to ROS 2 Humble in 4 steps.

## 1. Clone and install ROS

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RainbowRobotics/RBQ.git
cd RBQ

# Install ROS 2 Humble (first time) — https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/Installation/Ubuntu-Install-Debs.html
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y ros-humble-desktop \
    python3-colcon-common-extensions python3-rosdep \
    ros-humble-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp ros-humble-cyclonedds
sudo rosdep init && rosdep update
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
```

## 2. Build the ROS2 SDK

```bash
cd rbq_sdk/ros2
rosdep install --from-paths src -y --ignore-src
colcon build --symlink-install
source install/setup.bash
cd ../..
```

## 3. Run

**Simulation:**
```bash
source rbq_sdk/ros2/install/setup.bash
bash scripts/sim.bash
```

**Real robot:**

The robot's onboard software (`Network`) already speaks ROS 2-compatible DDS — there is **no driver node to launch**. Just source the workspace and configure DDS (next step) to reach the robot over the network.

```bash
source rbq_sdk/ros2/install/setup.bash
```

> The legacy `rbq_driver` node and `scripts/start_ros_driver.bash` are removed — the script is now a deprecated no-op.

## 4. DDS setup (developer PC ↔ robot Wi-Fi)

Set in the terminal you use for `ros2 topic` commands:

```bash
export CYCLONEDDS_URI='<CycloneDDS><Domain><Id>0</Id><General><Interfaces><NetworkInterface name="wlp4s0"/></Interfaces></General></Domain></CycloneDDS>'
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
```

Replace `wlp4s0` with your Wi-Fi interface (`ifconfig` to check).

## Quick command test

```bash
# Enable HighLevel Command mode
ros2 topic pub --once /rbq/cmd/switch_control_mode std_msgs/msg/Bool "{data: true}"

# Stand up
ros2 topic pub --once /rbq/cmd/switch_gait std_msgs/msg/Int8 "{data: 1}"

# Walk forward 0.3 m/s
ros2 topic pub --once /rbq/cmd/high_level rbq_msgs/msg/HighLevelCommand \
'{vel_x: 0.3, vel_y: 0.0, omega_z: 0.0, gait_state: 3, gait_transition: false}'

# Check topics
ros2 topic list
```

## List available topics

```bash
source rbq_sdk/ros2/install/setup.bash
ros2 topic list
```

→ **Full ROS2 reference**: [ROS2 SDK Overview](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/ros/overview.html)

SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/downloads/

## Docking Mode
In this mode, the robot autonomously aligns itself with the charging station.

- 🤖 The robot will stop any locomotion and begin charging once docked.

- ⚠️ Do not manually move the robot while in docking mode.

- Ensure the docking station is properly positioned and powered.

## RL (Vision Trot) Mode
In this mode, the robot uses a vision-based Reinforcement Learning policy to walk. It is trained to respond dynamically to terrain using onboard camera input.

- Ideal for uneven terrain or dynamic obstacles.

- May have different responsiveness compared to manually programmed gait modes.

<br>

## Walking Parameter Setting

Customize Your Robot’s Gait in Real Time

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2DynPHB6U64" title="Walking parameter setting" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Walking parameter setting</figcaption>
</figure>

You can fine-tune the walking behavior via the GUI:
- **Max Command Speed**   - Limits how fast the robot walks

- **Body Height** - Adjust vertical posture for clearance

- **Foot Height** - Controls how high the feet lift during swing phase

<img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/walking-parameter-set.png' alt='Walking parameter settings in GUI' />
