# GUI Software Update

This page explains how to update the GUI software from RBQGUI.

1. Make sure the internet connection is working.  
   (You must connect to a Wi-Fi network with internet access, not the robot network.)
   Press the Settings button in the top-left to open the settings screen.

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
    <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/gui-update-1.png' alt='Check internet connection' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
    <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Check internet connection</figcaption>
   </figure>

2. On the `Software Update` screen, check the current GUI version (RBQGUI) and the available target versions.

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/gui-update-2.png' alt='Current GUI version / target selection' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Current GUI / Target version</figcaption>
   </figure>

3. Select the desired version from the dropdown and click `DOWNLOAD`.  
   (Versions marked with a check mark are already downloaded.)

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/gui-update-3.png' alt='Select version' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Select version</figcaption>
   </figure>

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/gui-update-4.png' alt='DOWNLOAD' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">DOWNLOAD</figcaption>
   </figure>

4. After downloading, click `INSTALL APP`.

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/gui-update-5.png' alt='INSTALL APP' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">INSTALL APP</figcaption>
   </figure>

5. After installation completes, the installation log is displayed.  
   Check the updated RBQGUI version on the screen.

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/gui-update-6.png' alt='GUI installation complete' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Installation complete</figcaption>
   </figure>

## Notes / Warnings

- Check safety if `EMERGENCY` is shown.
- Updates can take time depending on the network condition.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/introduction.html
================================================================================

# RBQGUI

## Downloads {#downloads}

RBQGUI installers (Linux AppImage / Android APK) are available from the **[Downloads](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/downloads/)** page.

## Introduction

**RBQGUI** is the dedicated application to remotely control and monitor the RBQ quadruped from a PC or handheld controller. After connecting to the robot, you can change posture (sit, stand, walk, etc.) and inspect the environment using the 3D virtual view or camera video.

<ul style="margin-bottom: 0.75rem; padding-left: 1.25rem;">
  <li><strong>Connection</strong>: Communicates with the robot on the same network.</li>
  <li><strong>Control</strong>: Select gait modes, stair, docking, etc., and drive motion with the joystick.</li>
  <li><strong>Monitoring</strong>: View battery and connection status on screen.</li>
</ul>

<p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0.35rem;">Below is a representative screen after launching RBQGUI.</p>

<figure style="margin-top: 0; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/introduction.png' alt='RBQGUI main screen' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; transform: scale(1); transform-origin: center top;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem;">&lt;RBQGUI main screen&gt;</figcaption>
</figure>

## Button reference (1-9)

| No. | Function |
|---:|---|
| 1 | `Sit` mode: keep the robot in a sitting pose |
| 2 | `Stance` mode: stand up to the default pose |
| 3 | `Walk` mode: walk (forward/back, strafe, turn) |
| 4 | `Stair` mode: gait suited for stairs |
| 5 | `Docking` mode: align to the charging dock |
| 6 | `RL (Vision Trot)` mode: vision-based RL walking |
| 7 | `Walking Parameter Setting` mode: tune speed, body height, foot lift, etc. |
| 8 | `3D Virtual View` mode: switch to the 3D virtual view |
| 9 | `Camera View` mode: switch to the live camera view |

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>When posture or the app view changes, the corresponding button turns orange.</p>
</div>
</div>

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/ptz-gui.html
================================================================================

# PTZ GUI

If a PTZ camera (optional) is installed, you can control the camera direction (Pan/Tilt), zoom, and video mode (Thermal/Color) from RBQGUI.

## 1) Screen entry

1. Run RBQGUI and connect to the robot.
2. Move to the camera screen, then open the PTZ control screen.
3. When the PTZ is connected normally, you can use the control area at the bottom.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/ptz-1.png' alt='PTZ GUI main screen' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">PTZ GUI main screen</figcaption>
</figure>

## 2) Basic operation (Pan/Tilt)

- Drag the PTZ control area (virtual joystick) on the screen to move the camera left/right (Pan) and up/down (Tilt).
- When you release your hand, input stops. If needed, drag again for fine adjustments.
- For more accurate positioning, move slowly using smaller inputs instead of fast movements.

## 3) Zoom control

Use the bottom `Zoom` buttons to change the optical zoom immediately.

- `1x`, `3x`, `8x`, `16x`, `32x`: fixed zoom selection
- `Center`: return the camera direction to the default center position

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/ptz-2.png' alt='PTZ zoom and switch control' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Zoom buttons and switch area</figcaption>
</figure>

## 4) Video mode & joystick

On the bottom-right, you can control the **Thermal/Color** switch and the virtual joystick display.

- **Thermal / Color**: switch between thermal (`Thermal`) and color (`Color`) video
- **Joystick icon** (center of the right side of the screen): tap to show/hide the virtual joystick panel

## 5) Exit

Press the `Exit` button at the top-right to close the PTZ screen and return to the basic GUI screen.

## Demo video

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 1rem 0;">
  <iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/ThilVsiWMfc" title="PTZ basic operation" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">PTZ basic operation</figcaption>
</figure>

SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/robot-software-update.html

# Robot Software Update

This page explains how to update robot software from RBQGUI.

1. On the `Software Update` screen, check the current robot version and whether `UPDATE ROBOT` is enabled. Make sure Wi-Fi is connected between the robot and RBQGUI.

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/robot-update-1.png' alt='UPDATE ROBOT' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">UPDATE ROBOT</figcaption>
   </figure>

2. Transfer/install runs, and when finished, a success message and logs are shown.

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/robot-update-2.png' alt='Robot update progress / success' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Update complete / logs</figcaption>
   </figure>

3. A restart confirmation dialog will be shown.  
   The robot must be in **sitting** state, and you should not move the robot before restarting.

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/robot-update-3.png' alt='Restart Robot confirmation' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Restart Robot (YES/NO)</figcaption>
   </figure>

4. After restart, the Robot version is displayed as the updated value.

   <figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
     <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/robot-update-4.png' alt='Robot update complete confirmation' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
     <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Update complete confirmation</figcaption>
   </figure>

## Notes / Warnings

- Check safety if `EMERGENCY` is shown.
- Updates can take time depending on the network condition.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/state-monitoring.html
================================================================================

# State Monitoring

In RBQGUI, you can check the robot’s current status (emergency/power/sensors/perception modules) in real time.

## 1) Top Status Area

You can check the `EMERGENCY` status and various system status icons (battery/connection/power, etc.) at a glance.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/state-monitoring-1.png' alt='Top status area' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Top status area</figcaption>
</figure>

## 2) Diagnostic Table (Motors/IMU, etc.)

Review diagnostic values per leg/joint (e.g., HRR/HRP/...) along with temperature, gyro, and acceleration (ACC) readings in a table.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/state-monitoring-2.png' alt='Diagnostic table' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Joint/Sensor diagnostic table</figcaption>
</figure>

### Joint Naming

Joint IDs in the diagnostic table use the following abbreviations:

- **HRR** : Hind Right Roll, **HRP** : Hind Right Pitch, **HRK** : Hind Right Knee
- **HLR** : Hind Left Roll, **HLP** : Hind Left Pitch, **HLK** : Hind Left Knee
- **FRR** : Front Right Roll, **FRP** : Front Right Pitch, **FRK** : Front Right Knee
- **FLR** : Front Left Roll, **FLP** : Front Left Pitch, **FLK** : Front Left Knee

## 3) Perception Status

Check the ON/OFF state and operation status, errors, and Fail/Count information for perception-related modules such as the IR projector, night vision, and LED buzzer.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/state-monitoring-3.png' alt='Perception status' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Perception module status</figcaption>
</figure>

## 4) Power Switch & Module Check

You can check power switch states (Vision Computer/Cameras/sensors such as LiDAR) and review major power/load status like BAT/LEGS/ADDON/EXTERN/CHARGE. Press the button to refresh the status.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/state-monitoring-4.png' alt='Power switch and module check' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Power switch & module check</figcaption>
</figure>

## Notes / Warnings

- If `EMERGENCY` or an abnormal state is shown, secure safety first and then check the cause (sensor/power/perception module operation, etc.).
- If perception/sensor modules are OFF, the corresponding features (e.g., vision-based walking) may be limited.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/usb-software-update.html
================================================================================

# Software Update over USB

This page explains how to update the GUI and the robot software from a USB drive, for closed
networks with no internet access. You stage the installer files on a USB drive from an
internet-connected PC, then plug that drive into the Steam Deck or tablet you want to update.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>A USB update replaces the <strong>internet connection only</strong>. To update the robot software, the GUI must still be <strong>connected to the robot over Wi-Fi</strong>. Installing the GUI app alone does not require a robot connection.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Step 1. Stage the files on the USB drive {#prepare-usb}

On an internet-connected PC, plug in the USB drive and create an `RBQGUI` folder at its root.
Inside it, create a `v{version}` folder named after the version you want to install.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/usb-file-1.png' alt='Version folders inside the RBQGUI folder on a USB drive' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Version folders inside RBQGUI</figcaption>
</figure>

Download the two files for that version into the version folder. Both are available from the
[Downloads](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/downloads/) page.

| File | Purpose | Where to get it |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `RBQ-{version}.tar.gz` | Robot software | `Source code (tar.gz)` on the release |
| `RBQGUI.apk` | GUI app | Release attachment |

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/usb-file-2.png' alt='The tar.gz and apk files inside a version folder' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Installer files inside a version folder</figcaption>
</figure>

Staging several versions in advance lets you pick the one you need in the field.

## Step 2. Plug in the drive and scan for versions {#scan-usb}

Plug the prepared USB drive into the Steam Deck or tablet you want to update, then press
**`USB`** on the `Software Update` screen.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/update-gui-usb-1.png' alt='The USB button on the Software Update screen' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">USB button</figcaption>
</figure>

The log pane reports how many versions the scan found.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/update-gui-usb-2.png' alt='Scan result shown in the log pane' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Scan complete</figcaption>
</figure>

## Step 3. Select the version to install {#select-version}

Open the version dropdown and select the version you want. Versions found on the USB drive are
marked **`[USB]`**.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/update-gui-usb-3.png' alt='Version list with [USB] markers' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Selecting a version found on USB</figcaption>
</figure>

Everything up to this point is the same for both updates. The steps below differ by target.

## Step 4 (GUI). Install the GUI app {#install-gui}

Press **`Install App`** to install the GUI from `RBQGUI.apk` on the drive.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/update-gui-usb-4.png' alt='Install App button' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Install App</figcaption>
</figure>

When the install finishes, check that `RBQGUI` under `Current Software Version` at the top of
the screen now shows the version you installed.

## Step 4 (Robot). Send the robot software {#update-robot}

Press **`Update Robot`**. The `RBQ-{version}.tar.gz` file is copied from the drive to the
device, then transferred to the robot.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/update-robot-usb-4.png' alt='Update Robot button' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Update Robot</figcaption>
</figure>

When the transfer completes, a success message appears along with a **`Restart Robot`** button.
The log shows the copy-from-USB step followed by the transfer to the robot.

<figure style="margin-top: 1rem; text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/gui/update-robot-usb-5.png' alt='Restart Robot button shown after a completed transfer' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">Transfer complete · Restart Robot</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Put the robot in the <strong>sitting</strong> state before restarting, and do not move it until the restart finishes.</p>
</div>
</div>

Restart the robot with `Restart Robot`, then check that `ROBOT` under
`Current Software Version` now shows the version you installed.

## Notes

- The version folder name must start with `v` and match the version in the `tar.gz` filename
  inside it.
- Updating the robot requires the GUI to be connected to the robot. Installing the GUI app does
  not.
- If `EMERGENCY` appears during an update, check safety immediately.

## Related pages

| Topic | Link |
|:---|:---|
| GUI update over the internet | [GUI Software Update](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/gui-software-update.html) |
| Robot update over the internet | [Robot Software Update](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/gui/robot-software-update.html) |

# Coordinate Frames (TF)

This page collects the **base-to-sensor transform matrices (TF)** for every sensor mounted on
the RBQ. Each matrix is a 4×4 homogeneous transform from the robot base frame to the sensor
frame; translation components are in **meters (m)**.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>These are <strong>fixed mounting transforms</strong>. Transforms that change at runtime (<code>odom → base_link</code>, leg joints, and so on) are broadcast by the robot on <code>/tf</code> — see the <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/software/sdk/ros/topics.html#tf">ROS 2 topic reference</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>

# Rail & spring nut

The robot uses **rails** for mounting optional hardware such as **PTZ cameras**, **LiDAR** units, and related brackets. **Spring nuts** inserted into the rail slot provide threaded anchor points for bolts.

## Purchase links

| Region | MISUMI product page |
|--------|----------------------|
| South Korea | [SHNTP5-5 (kr.misumi-ec.com)](https://kr.misumi-ec.com/vona2/detail/110302608410/?HissuCode=SHNTP5-5&PNSearch=SHNTP5-5&searchFlow=results2products&list=PageSearchResult) |
| United States | [SHNTP5-5 (us.misumi-ec.com)](https://us.misumi-ec.com/vona2/detail/110302247640/?PNSearch=SHNTP5-5&HissuCode=SHNTP5-5&seriesCode=110302247640&tab=drawingAndSpecifications&Page=1) |

## Inserting a spring nut

1. **Insert at an angle.** Slide the spring nut **diagonally** into the rail slot so it enters the internal channel.
2. **Press the part that sticks out.** A portion of the nut may sit **proud of the slot**; press it so the nut seats fully in the channel.
3. **Align with the rail.** Adjust the nut so it is **aligned with the slot** and can slide along the rail as needed.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/insert-1.png' alt='Insert spring nut diagonally into the rail' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 1 - diagonal insert</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/insert-2.png' alt='Press the portion protruding outside the rail' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 2 - press the protruding section</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/insert-3.png' alt='Align the nut with the rail slot' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 3 - align with the slot</figcaption>
</figure>

## Removing a spring nut

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p><strong>Tool diameter</strong></p>
<p>Use a rigid rod <strong>no larger than 4 mm</strong> in diameter. A thicker tool can damage the nut or mar the rail slot.</p>
</div>
</div>

1. **Insert a rod into the nut.** Pass a **rigid rod** (**≤ 4 mm** diameter) through the hole in the spring nut.
2. **Push to one wall.** Push the nut **against one inner wall** of the rail slot.
3. **Twist and lift.** While holding it against that wall, **twist and lift** the nut toward the **opposite** side of the slot so it can clear the profile and release from the rail.
4. **Remove.** Withdraw the nut from the slot.

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/remove-1.png' alt='Insert rod into spring nut hole' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 1 - rod through the hole</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/remove-2.png' alt='Push nut against one wall of the rail' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 2 - push to one wall</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/remove-3.png' alt='Twist and lift away from the wall' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 3 - twist and lift</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/remove-4.png' alt='Remove spring nut from rail' style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 100%; height: auto;" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">Step 4 - remove</figcaption>
</figure>

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/hardware/specification.html

# External Port Information

## Overall External Port Panel

There are two panel layouts — **version 1** and **version 2** — and which one your robot
has depends on the robot. The quickest way to tell them apart is the pair of USB-C ports
on the right edge: version 1 labels them **VISION / MOTION**, version 2 labels them
**U-PC / R-PC**. They are the same two ports — version 2 names the PC each one reaches
instead of its role.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>The panel layout can differ between versions. Please <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/troubleshooting/error-reporting.html">contact us</a> if you are unsure which one your robot has.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="rbq-compare">
  <figure id="panel-v1">
    <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/port-panel-v1.png' alt='External port panel, version 1' />
    <figcaption>Version 1</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure id="panel-v2">
    <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/port-panel-v2.png' alt='External port panel, version 2' />
    <figcaption>Version 2</figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>

### Ports by version {#ports-by-version}

| Port | Version 1 | Version 2 |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Power | `POWER` | `POWER` |
| Power · CAN | `PWR-CAN` | `PWR/CAN` |
| Power · LAN | `12V-LAN` ×3 | `12V/LAN` ×3 |
| LiDAR | `LiDAR` | No dedicated port — use `12V/LAN` |
| Emergency stop | `EMO` | `EMO` |
| USB-C (direct to PC) | `VISION`, `MOTION` | `U-PC`, `R-PC` |

## Charging & Power Switch

Both versions carry the same three elements — the power port with its cover, the power
button, and the robot status lights — but lay them out differently.

<div class="rbq-compare">
  <figure>
    <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/power-switch-v1.png' alt='Charging and power switch, version 1' />
    <figcaption>Version 1</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure>
    <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/power-switch-v2.png' alt='Charging and power switch, version 2' />
    <figcaption>Version 2</figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>

| Element | Version 1 | Version 2 |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Power port cover | Hinged flip cover | Screw-down round cover |
| Robot status lights | Horizontal strip above the power port | Vertical strip beside the power button |
| Power button | Below the power port | Bottom left, next to the status lights |

<p>- Robot Battery Lights</p>
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/battery-lights.png' alt='Robot battery indicator lights' style="width: 400px;" />
</figure>

<p>- Robot Status Lights (blinking)</p>
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/status-lights.png' alt='Robot status indicator lights' style="width: 500px;" />
</figure>

<p>- Power Button Status</p>
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/button-status.png' alt='Power button status' style="width: 400px;" />

## Direct PC Port

Two USB-C ports connect straight to the onboard PCs. They are the same two ports on both
versions; only the labels changed.

<div class="rbq-compare">
  <figure>
    <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/pc-port-v1.png' alt='Direct PC ports, version 1' />
    <figcaption>Version 1</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure>
    <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/pc-port-v2.png' alt='Direct PC ports, version 2' />
    <figcaption>Version 2</figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>

| Connects to | Version 1 | Version 2 |
|:---|:---|:---|
| User PC | `VISION` | `U-PC` |
| Robot PC | `MOTION` | `R-PC` |

# Network Configuration Diagram

The network layout differs from robot to robot. Two things vary:

- **Configuration** — the **research** layout keeps the User PC outside the robot and treats payloads as one generic LAN group. The **industrial** layout mounts the User PC inside the robot and wires each payload individually.
- **Router** — some robots have the router **integrated into the switch hub**, so the LTE/5G · Wi-Fi (Mesh) module connects straight to it. Others reach the network through a **separate external router**.

In every diagram, **R-PC** is the robot's motion PC and **U-PC** is the user PC. Green lines are LAN, orange lines are WAN.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>The network layout can differ between versions. Please <a href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/troubleshooting/error-reporting.html">contact us</a> if you are unsure which one applies to your robot.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Research configuration

The U-PC sits outside the robot. LAN payloads — LiDAR, PTZ camera, RTK GPS and so on — share a single connection to the switch hub.

### Router integrated into the switch hub

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/network-diagram-1.png' alt='Network configuration diagram, research configuration, router integrated into the switch hub' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Research · Router integrated ]</figcaption>
</figure>

### Separate external router

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/network-diagram-4.png' alt='Network configuration diagram, research configuration, separate external router' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Research · External router ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Industrial configuration

The U-PC is mounted inside the robot alongside the R-PC, and each payload — LiDAR 1, LiDAR 2, PTZ camera — has its own connection to the switch hub.

### Router integrated into the switch hub

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/network-diagram-2.png' alt='Network configuration diagram, industrial configuration, router integrated into the switch hub' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Industrial · Router integrated ]</figcaption>
</figure>

### Separate external router

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/interface/network-diagram-3.png' alt='Network configuration diagram, industrial configuration, separate external router' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Industrial · External router ]</figcaption>
</figure>

On this layout LiDAR 2 connects through the router rather than directly to the switch hub.

## Network details

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Wi-Fi | 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz |
| Network switch speed | Gigabit Ethernet (1 Gbps) |
| Access point | `192.168.0.1` |

## Onboard PCs and IP addresses

Every robot ships with the Motion PC (R-PC). The Vision PC and the User PC (U-PC) are
options — your robot may not have them.

| PC | IP | Role | Fitted | User access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Motion PC (R-PC) | `192.168.0.10` | Robot control | Standard | No |
| Vision PC | `192.168.0.12` | Vision processing | Option | No |
| User PC (U-PC) | `192.168.0.13` | Your development work | Option | Yes |

The Motion PC and the Vision PC run the robot itself and are not user-accessible. Do your
development work on the U-PC.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">If the U-PC does not respond</p>
<p>The U-PC default address is <code>192.168.0.13</code>. If you cannot connect, attach a monitor to the U-PC and check its current IP. If it is using a different address, set it statically to <code>192.168.0.13</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/maintenance/battery.html
================================================================================

# Battery Replacement

## How to detach batteries

<div class="sb sb-danger">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">DANGER</p>
<p><strong>Bare-hand contact</strong> with battery terminals or connectors can cause shock, short circuit, burns, or fire. Always wear <strong>insulating gloves</strong> when detaching or attaching. Confirm power is fully off.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Before detaching, confirm the RBQ10 is <strong>sitting down</strong> and <strong>powered off</strong>. Otherwise the robot may move or fall, which can escalate to a more severe incident.</p>
</div>
</div>

The batteries are located on the sides of the RBQ10.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/bat-1.png' alt='Battery location and side covers' />
</figure>

Before opening the latches of the RBQ10, the front legs must be lifted up for clearance.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>When lifting the legs or operating the latches and battery cover, keep <strong>fingers and hands clear of gaps</strong> between legs, body, and cover. Pulling or pushing a lever while your hand is in the gap can cause injury. <strong>Support or hold</strong> the part with one hand and operate levers and covers with the other only.</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/bat-2.png' alt='Battery latch levers and detaching' />
</figure>

The levers are on the sides of the battery latches and pulling all four of them releases the battery from the body. After releasing the latches, pull the battery cover to detach the battery.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/bat-3.png' alt='Battery removal step' />
</figure>

## How to attach batteries

To attach the batteries, push the battery into the robot body and place the hook into the groove. Then, firmly press the levers to fix the battery.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/bat-4.png' alt='Battery installation and locking' />
</figure>

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/maintenance/bumper.html
================================================================================

# Stand & Bumper Replacement

The stand that supports the body of the RBQ10 when it is in a standby sitting position, and the front and rear bumpers that absorb impact when the robot falls, wear out with use and need to be replaced. The replacement method is as follows, so please refer to it if necessary.

## Stand replacement

The stand of the RBQ10 consists of M4x10mm hex-wrench bolts and M4 flat washers. If any parts are lost during disassembly, you can purchase replacements of the same specifications.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/stand-bumper-1.png' alt='Stand and bumper replacement 1' />
</figure>

### Step 1. Unscrew the bolt using a 3mm hex wrench.

### Step 2. Pull out the urethane stand and replace it with a new component.

### Step 3. Fasten the bolt. (Apply Loctite 243 to the bolt thread)

## Front & rear bumpers

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/stand-bumper-2.png' alt='Stand and bumper replacement 2' />
</figure>

3 sets of M3x10mm bolts and M4 flat washers attach the bumper to the robot.

Use a 2.5mm hexagonal wrench to loosen the bolts.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/maintenance/connector.html
================================================================================

# Connector Attachment/Detachment

The RBQ10 interface connector uses MOCO's F-series waterproof connector. Once the connector is engaged, it cannot be disconnected by vibration or pulling the wire. To remove the connector, you need to hold the handle and pull it to safely detach it without damage.

### Step 1. Grab the handle.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Applying force to the wires outside the handle area may cause damage.</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/connector-1.png' alt='Connector detachment 1' />
</figure>

### Step 2. Align the red dots and press the connector handle until it clicks.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/connector-2.png' alt='Connector detachment 2' />
</figure>


### Step 3. Check connection.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/connector-3.png' alt='Connector detachment 3' />
</figure>

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/maintenance/foot.html
================================================================================

# Foot Replacement

The rubber feet of the RBQ10 wear down with use. If the feet are significantly worn, they need to be replaced. The replacement process is as follows.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/foot-1.png' alt='Foot module replacement overview' />
</figure>

### Step 1. Unscrew the bolt using a 4mm hex wrench.


### Step 2. Remove the foot covers and pull the rubber foot.


### Step 3. Replace the foot with a new component.


### Step 4. Fasten the bolts to the cover. (Apply Loctite 243 before fastening)

# Leg module Attachment/Detachment

This manual explains the disassembly and assembly sequence of the RBQ10 leg module. The instructions are based on the front left leg, and since the other legs have a symmetrical structure, the same method should be used for the disassembly and assembly process.

<b>Fastening specification</b>

<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Parameter</th>
    <th>Specification</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Hex wrench</td>
    <td>4mm</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Q’ty</td>
    <td>6 bolts in total</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Spring washer</td>
    <td>M5</td>
  </tr>
</table>

## Leg module disassembly

The bolts fastening the leg module are placed as shown below.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/leg-1.png' alt='Leg module bolt layout' />
</figure>

### Step 1. Unscrew the bolts. (Dispose of the used M5 spring washers)

### Step 2. Pull the leg module outward after the bolts are unscrewed.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Be careful not to damage the com-wire by pulling it too far.</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/leg-2.png' alt='Leg module removal' />
</figure>

### Step 3. Pull the connector handle to release the com-wire.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Pulling the com-wire directly may cause disconnection. Make sure to pull the handle.</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/leg-3.png' alt='Com-wire connector location' />
</figure>
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/leg-4.png' alt='Com-wire released by pulling the handle' />
</figure>

## Leg module assembly

The leg com-wire must be coiled once before assembly. If it is assembled without coiling, the com-wire may get pinched and damaged between the leg and the upper and lower plates.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>The spring washer for the bolts securing the leg is crucial for proper fastening. Be careful not to forget it during assembly.</p>
</div>
</div>

### Step 1. Coil the com-wire as shown in the picture below.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/leg-5.png' alt='Coiling the com-wire' />
</figure>

### Step 2. Align the red dots and press firmly to connect the com-wire.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Pushing the com-wire may cause disconnection. Make sure to press the handle.</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/leg-6.png' alt='Connector mating' />
</figure>

### Step 3. Insert the roll frame and reducer slot into the body frame.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/leg-7.png' alt='Insert roll frame' />
</figure>

### Step 4. Fasten the bolts. (Make sure to insert the M5 spring washers)

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/maintenance/leg-8.png' alt='Tighten leg module bolts' />
</figure>

# Charging

The RBQ10 can be charged using the supplied charger or docking station. The charger uses the charging port on the top of the robot; the docking station charges through the port on the bottom. You can also connect a charging cable to the docking station and then connect it to the charging port on the top of the robot to charge.

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>Charge the robot only with the supplied RBQ10 charger or RBQ10 docking station.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Charging with the RBQ10 charger

<figure>

## Charging with the docking station

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/description-1.png" alt="Docking station parts" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Docking station ]</figcaption>
</figure>

### How to charge

#### Step 1: Position the robot so the front or rear camera faces the docking station.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/manual-1.png" alt="Manual docking step 1 placement" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Docking step 1 ]</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-required">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-book" aria-hidden="true">📖</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">REQUIRED READING</p>
<p>The distance between the docking station and the robot must be within 5 meters, and the front or rear camera must be able to recognize ArUco markers before automatic docking is possible.</p>
</div>
</div>

#### Step 2: Press the `Docking` button.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/docking-manual-2.png" alt="Docking button location" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Docking button ]</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>When the robot recognizes a QR code, the docking sequence starts automatically.</p>
</div>
</div>

#### Step 3: The robot automatically attempts docking and, on failure, automatically retries.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(500px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-7.png" alt="Charging on docking station" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Charging with docking station ]</figcaption>
</figure>

### Charging status

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-8.png" alt="Docking station status display" />

<div class="image-group" style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; text-align: center; margin-top: 1rem; margin-bottom: 1rem;">

### How to charge

#### Step 1: Connect the external charging cable to the RBQ10 docking station external charging port.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-4.png" alt="Docking external cable step 1" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Connect cable to external charging port ]</figcaption>
</figure>

#### Step 2: Connect the external charging cable to the RBQ10 charging port.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-2.png" alt="Cable to robot charge port step 2" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Connect cable to robot charging port ]</figcaption>
</figure>

#### Step 3: Charge the RBQ10 using the docking station external charging cable.

<figure>
  <img style="max-width: 100%; width: min(700px, 100%); height: auto; display: block; margin: 1rem auto; border-radius: 8px;" src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/charging/charging-6.png" alt="Charging via dock external cable step 3" />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Charge robot with external cable ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Docking station installation precautions

1. The charging station is water-resistant, but if water is present on the charging terminals, charging problems may occur; install it away from places where water splashes.
2. The power cable is treated for water exposure, but when connecting to an external outlet, keep water out of the plug connection.
3. Prolonged direct sunlight can cause overheating; installing in a shaded location is recommended.
4. Secure the charging station to the floor using the fixing holes.

# Controller (Steam Deck) and Wi-Fi Connection

This page describes how to connect the STEAM DECK to the robot Wi-Fi, communicate with the robot in RBQGUI, and proceed through auto start. Complete [Robot Initial Pose Setting](./initial-pose) (initial pose and power on) first.

## Step 1: Open RBQGUI app

Run the `RBQGUI` app from the STEAM DECK desktop.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-open-app.png' alt='RBQGUI app' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ RBQGUI app ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Step 2: Wi-Fi connection

The robot provides a Wi-Fi access point named `RBQ_{XX}` (XX differs by unit). Connect the STEAM DECK to that network.

1. **Check Wi-Fi** - After connecting the Steam Deck to the robot AP (`RBQ_{XX}`), confirm the **top-right** of RBQGUI shows the network name and signal icon.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-wifi-1.png' alt='Wi-Fi status in RBQGUI' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Wi-Fi menu ]</figcaption>
</figure>

2. **Select the robot network** - Choose `RBQ_{XX}` in the list. (If it does not appear, check robot power and Wi-Fi operation.)

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-wifi-2.png' alt='Select RBQ_XX network' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Select RBQ_{XX} ]</figcaption>
</figure>

3. **Verify connection** - Confirm the deck shows **Connected** to `RBQ_{XX}`.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-wifi-3.png' alt='RBQ_XX connected' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Wi-Fi connected ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Step 3: Connect STEAM DECK and robot

For RBQGUI to talk to the robot, you must also establish remote controller-robot communication inside the app.

1. **Open the connection dialog** - Press `Remote Controller-Robot Communication Connection` (orange) on the left of the top bar. A connection pop-up appears.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-connect-1.png' alt='Remote controller-robot communication connection' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Communication connection button and pop-up ]</figcaption>
</figure>

2. **Connect** - In the pop-up, press `Connect` to attempt communication with the robot.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-connect-2.png' alt='Connect button' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Connect ]</figcaption>
</figure>

3. **Confirm result** - When connected, `Remote Controller-Robot Communication Connection` at the same position turns **green**, and the pop-up shows a connected state.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/rc-connect-connect-3.png' alt='Connected to robot' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Connected (button green) ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Step 4: Auto start {#auto-start}

To bring up robot software and state in one flow, use the auto start procedure.

1. **Open initial setup** - Press `Robot Initial Setup` (red) on the left of the top bar.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/auto-start-1.png' alt='Robot Initial Setup' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Robot Initial Setup button ]</figcaption>
</figure>

2. **Run auto start** - In the pop-up, press `Auto Start Robot`. After a short wait, progress appears on screen.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/auto-start-2.png' alt='Auto Start Robot' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Auto Start Robot ]</figcaption>
</figure>

3. **Check progress** - Confirm each item such as `Manual Setup` updates. (Some items may show green before others for a while.)

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/auto-start-3.png' alt='Auto start in progress' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Auto start in progress ]</figcaption>
</figure>

4. **Confirm completion** - When **all** setup items shown on screen are **green**, auto start has completed successfully.

<figure style="text-align: center; margin: 0.5rem auto 1.25rem;">
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/auto-start-4.png' alt='Auto start complete' style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07);" />
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; color: var(--vp-c-text-2, #666); font-size: 0.95em;">[ Auto start complete (all green) ]</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-warning">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">WARNING</p>
<p>If, after auto start, not all setup items turn green or an error is shown, confirm no people are nearby, review the <a href="../Safety/emergency-stop-procedures">emergency stop procedures</a>, then follow the steps below. Before operation, always comply with the <a href="../Safety/general-safety-warning-precautions">general safety guidelines</a>.</p>
<ol style="margin: 0.5rem 0 0 1.25rem;">
<li>If <code>Check CAN-Bus</code> fails: power off the robot safely, then restart.</li>
<li>If <code>Find Home-pose</code> fails: on a flat, stable surface per <a href="../Safety/maintenance-safety">maintenance safety</a>, check leg pose, then restart.</li>
</ol>
<p style="margin-top: 0.75rem;">If the problem persists, contact Rainbow Robotics via <a href="../Troubleshooting/error-reporting">error reporting</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>

SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/operation/emo.html

# Emergency Stop and Recovery Procedures

## Emergency stop using the button

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/emo.png' alt='Emergency stop button on rear of robot' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ Emergency stop push button on the rear of the robot ]</figcaption>
</figure>

When the robot’s **emergency stop button** is pressed, all joints switch to **High Damping**. In this state, the robot’s legs resist external motion but **do not** accept torque or position commands.
This is a safety mode to protect the user and the robot in an emergency or unintended motion.

<div class="sb sb-note">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-note-i" aria-hidden="true">i</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">NOTE</p>
<p>During emergency stop, control is disabled and the robot may lose posture and settle to the ground under gravity.</p>
</div>
</div>

To recover from emergency stop:

1. Rotate the emergency stop button clockwise and return it to its original position.
2. Press the "Stance" button in the GUI, or perform [Robot Initial Pose Setting](https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/operation/initial-pose.html).
3. Follow the initialization steps to return the robot to a ready state.

This reinitializes joint control and robot posture correctly.

================================================================================
SOURCE: https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/operation/initial-pose.html
================================================================================

# Robot Initial Pose Setting

Place the robot on a flat floor so that all feet and knees contact the ground. Refer to the robot posture in the image below.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/initial-pose-1.png' alt='Initial pose setup step 1' />
  <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ RBQ10 Initial Pose ]</figcaption>
</figure>

## Step 1. A flat surface is required.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/initial-pose-2.png' alt='Initial pose setup step 2' />
</figure>

## Step 2. Fully fold the knee joint.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/initial-pose-3.png' alt='Initial pose setup step 3' />
</figure>

## Step 3. Rotate the hip pitch and roll joints so that the “feet” and “knee” joints touch the ground. There are three ground points. (Body Bumper, Knee Joint, Foot)

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/initial-pose-4.png' alt='Initial pose setup step 4' />
</figure>

## Turn On the Robot {#power-on}

<figure style="text-align: center;">
  <img src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/operation/power-button.png" alt="Power button" style="width: 300px;" />
</figure>

<p>- Press <strong>Power Button</strong> and check the red light on the button</p>
<p>- Check for <strong>double-beep sound</strong></p>

# Packing
The RBQ10 is primarily stored and transported using a Pelican case. The model of the Pelican case used is the 1730 Protector Case. Please refer to the images below and store the RBQ10 along with other items accordingly.


## Robot packing and unpacking
The Pelican case has two layers. The lower layer holds the charger, spare rubber feet, and LiDAR; the RBQ10 is placed on top of them.
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-1.png' alt='Pelican case lower layer layout' />
</figure>

After arranging items in the lower layer, carry the robot as shown in the figure and place it in the case.

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>The robot must be carried by two people working together.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Before transporting the robot, remove any additional equipment attached to it and turn off the power.</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-2.png' alt='Carrying robot into case' />
</figure>

After setting the RBQ10 on the floor, extend the legs as shown in the figure.

Two people should carry the robot, each holding one of the leg areas marked in red.

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-3.png' alt='Transport with legs extended' />
</figure>

<div class="sb sb-caution">
<div class="sb-icon"><span class="sb-warn" aria-hidden="true">⚠</span></div>
<div class="sb-content">
<p class="custom-block-title">CAUTION</p>
<p>Be careful not to let any foreign objects get into the knee joint rotation area, and ensure fingers do not get pinched!</p>
</div>
</div>

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-4.png' alt='Knee joint caution pose' />
</figure>

Place the robot in the Pelican 1730 case to match the case shape.

After the body is in the case, fold the legs in this order:

### Step 1: Fold the front legs’ knee joints fully
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-5.png' alt='Front leg knee fold step 1' />
</figure>

### Step 2: Rotate the front legs’ hip pitch joints and place the legs into the case recesses

<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-6.png' alt='Front leg hip pitch rotation step 2' />
</figure>
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-7.png' alt='Front leg placed in case step 2 (continued)' />
</figure>

### Step 3: Rotate the rear legs’ hip pitch joints so the legs go over the front thighs

### Step 4: Fully extend the rear shins
<figure>
  <img src='https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/packing/packing-8.png' alt='Rear leg shin extension step 4' />
</figure>

Place the remote controller in the side storage next to the robot. Remaining empty space can be used as needed.

Close the lid to finish packing.

Unpacking is the reverse of the above steps.

# Accessories

RBQ supports a range of optional accessories that extend the robot for field missions and
development work — sensing, onboard compute and connectivity, and power infrastructure.

## Sensing {#sensing}

<div class="rbq-card-grid">

  <div class="rbq-card">
    <img src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/hardware/ptz-camera.png" alt="" />
    <h3 id="ptz-camera">PTZ Camera<a class="header-anchor" href="#ptz-camera" aria-label="Permalink to PTZ Camera"></a></h3>
    <p>A Pan-Tilt-Zoom camera that mounts on the RBQ body. Provides high-resolution video streaming for surveillance and reconnaissance missions with remote pan, tilt, and zoom control via the GUI and API.</p>
    <a class="rbq-card-cta" href="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/manual/related-products/ptz-camera.html">Specifications →</a>
  </div>

  <div class="rbq-card">
    <img src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/images/accessories/mid-360.png" alt="" />
    <h3 id="lidar-mid-360">LIDAR (mid-360)<a class="header-anchor" href="#lidar-mid-360" aria-label="Permalink to LIDAR (mid-360)"></a></h3>
    <p>The Livox MID-360 is a compact 3D LiDAR with a hemispherical field of view (360° × 59°). Used for SLAM, obstacle detection, and autonomous navigation. Connects via Ethernet.</p>

# RBQ Series

Rainbow Robotics' RBQ quadruped series is designed to be easy for anyone to use. Based on dynamics-based gait control and learning-based locomotion, it can move stably in unstructured environments such as rough terrain, slopes, and stairs. With various sensors, interfaces, and payload options, it can be used for field-oriented missions such as surveillance, reconnaissance, and safety management.

As a development platform, RBQ provides diverse interfaces, APIs, and SDKs so users can easily develop, integrate, and test their own robot applications.

* **Durability:** With an IP54 rating and a highly durable mechanical structure, RBQ can operate reliably in harsh environments for extended periods.
* **Expandability:** Built-in expansion network interfaces and power outputs support additional equipment and sensors. It also provides a developer-friendly software environment for rapid prototyping and integration.
* **Mobility:** RBQ can be transported in a dedicated case using a standard vehicle. It is designed for easy handling during transport, setup, and operation.

<figure>
    <img
    src="https://rainbowrobotics.github.io/RBQ/nightly/RBQ_rendered.png" alt="RBQ quadruped robot" style="max-width: 100%; width: 480px; height: auto;"
    />
    <figcaption style="text-align: center;">[ RBQ 10 ]</figcaption>
</figure>

# Docking Station

The docking station helps RBQ automatically charge by moving to the charging station and executing a charging command when a mission is complete or the battery is low. With the docking station, the robot can repeatedly perform missions with minimal human intervention.
